recentItems.title: Police probe attempted arson attack on German defense firm | DW News
recentItems.description:

Further investigations are underway. German authorities are on high alert for attacks on infrastructure after the government accused Russia of being behind an attempted drone attack on Leipzig airport.

recentItems.title: Why is Russia coming for Germany? | Berlin Briefing Podcast
recentItems.description:
Germany has officially blamed Russia for a suspected hybrid attack at Leipzig airport. While Berlin has insisted the country is "not at war," the line between peace and conflict is becoming increasingly blurred — as attacks become bolder and more frequent. DW hosts Nina Haase and Max Hofmann discuss what this could mean for Germany, NATO and the wider West with DW Brussels Correspondent Teri Schultz and DW's Eastern Europe Security Correspondent Roman Goncharenko, examining Russia's moves, Germany's response, and whether hybrid warfare is entering a dangerous new stage.

recentItems.title: Live: World Meteorological Organization's El Nino update | DW News
recentItems.description:
The El Nino weather phenomenon looks set to strengthen into next year.  The periodic phenomenon that sees warming of sea temperatures in the eastern Pacific Ocean, could also be the strongest for 70 years. UN Secretary General Antonio Guterres says it is being ‘supersized before our eyes.’ Join us with your questions as we bring you a live update from the World Meteorological Organization on how El Nino is developing.

recentItems.title: Does Germany's secret ballistic missile test signal a shift in its defense strategy? | DW News
recentItems.description:
Germany has quietly tested one of the most advanced long-range ballistic missiles ever considered for its arsenal. The launch of Israel Aerospace Industries' LORA missile system took place in the North Atlantic and was kept under wraps until the last moment. The test comes as Berlin prepares a reported €12 billion missile program and publicly accuses Russia of involvement in an attempted drone attack near Leipzig Airport. Is Germany entering a new era of long-range ballistic military deterrence? We break down what the LORA can do and what this signals for European security.
DW speaks to Olaf Böhnke, Managing Director of Rasmussen Global, on Germany's shifting military strategy. 

Chapter Breakdown
0:00 Germany secretly tests long-range Israeli ballistic missile system 
0:50 German government preparing 12 billion euro missile program according to documents obtained by POLITICO
1:18 LORA is a quasi-ballistic missile which can reach supersonic speeds, can strike targets at speeds faster than conventional cruise missiles
1:54 German navy chief statement
2:16 Olaf Böhnke on the Israeli LORA ballistic missile system
3:15 Germany does not currently have ballistic missiles and will go ahead with procurement of LORA
5:21 Why did Germany publicly announce conducting this test now, right after officials blamed Russia for an attempted drone attack at Leipzig airport
7:14 Germany building up missile program to the amount of 12 billion euros, money which still requires parliamentary approval
8:07 Germany now shaping military strategy around deterrence, while previous military efforts were focused on foreign deployment
10:24 How does this push toward long-range strike capabilities fit into the "Zeitenwende" or turning point in German defense?
13:20 Böhnke: Germany changed its Constitution to allow for increases in defense spending, and is no longer just a "consumer" of US' security umbrella, but a provider of security
15:28 Potential controversy around Germany procuring LORA from Israel, as well as testing technology in Israel-Palestine
16:56 Critics say more long-range missiles could drive escalation in Russia-Ukraine war

#dwnews #israelaerospaceindustries

recentItems.title: Bond market sell-off sends warning to countries running high debt | DW News
recentItems.description:
When governments spend beyond their means, they sell bonds to finance their debt.  It allows countries to kick the can of balanced budgets down the road, until they hit a dead end. Now a major sell-off on global bond markets is pushing borrowing costs higher and forcing some hard choices. Is bond market warning governments that the era of cheap money is coming to an end? What will be the impact on the global economy?

DW speaks to Carsten Brzeski, Global Head at Macro Research and Chief Economist at ING Germany, on US economic interventions

Chapter Breakdown
0:00 Why yields go up when bond prices go down
0:36 James Carville, strategist for establishment Democratic candidates, former Bill Clinton campaign strategist, on why the bond market is so consequential
0:52 US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announces bond buyback scheme
1:14 US President Trump on whether he directed Bessent to do the intervention
1:56 Markets react to US debt (40 trillion USD) and the war in Iran, with 10-year US Treasury yields approaching 5% and Japanese, German, and UK borrowing costs also increasing
2:22 Carsten Brzeski, former employee at the Dutch Finance Ministry and European Commission, on Trump's comments impyling the US military can solve economic issues
3:07 How does American military power and dollar dominance go hand in hand?
3:56 Brzeski argues that US dollar hegemony is not (yet) over
#dwcurrentaffairs #bondmarket #scottbessent 
5:31 Why the war in Iran has pushed up energy prices and rates
6:05 Bessent's unusual bond intervention: why Treasuries typically do not intervene in capital markets
7:12 Interventions such as Bessent's only work if accompanied by fiscal policy changes
7:20 Can markets ignore worsening public deficits?
7:46 Markets "repricing" their inflation expectations, given their realization that the US is in a "forever" war in Iran
9:09 "End of the welfare state" with rising spending on defence in Germany

recentItems.title: Why is China courting key US military ally in the Middle East? | DW News
recentItems.description:
Chinese President Xi Jinping is visiting Egypt - his first trip to the Middle East in four years. Beijing is seeking to expand its influence as US partners in the region have been reassessing their strategic relationships over the war against Iran. Analyst H.A. Hellyer explains what he sees as a 'diversification of relationships' by Egypt and other players in the region.

00:00 Xi visits Egypt amid US-Israeli war on Iran
